rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks to be sincere servants of God, or to submit and obey; it requests increased sincerity and submission, or steadfastness in them.
rows.anchor: مخلصين لك، من أسلم وجهه، أو مستسلمين من أسلم إذا استسلم وانقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading takes “Muslims” to mean the two petitioners and Hajar, or treats the dual as one rank within the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { مسلمين } على أن المراد أنفسهما وهاجر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask that some of their descendants be a community submitted to God; they specify descendants out of compassion and because their reform benefits their followers.
rows.anchor: وإنما خصا الذرية بالدعاء لأنهم أحق بالشفقة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for only some descendants because they know some will be unjust and divine wisdom does not require universal devotion, which would disrupt worldly life.
rows.anchor: وخصا بعضهم لما أعلما أن في ذريتهما ظلمة، وعلما أن الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible referent of the community is Muhammad’s community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالأمة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may explain “community,” delayed before its clarified noun and separating conjunction from what it coordinates, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون من للتبيين كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arinā derives from seeing or knowing; on either sense its verb does not take more than two objects.
rows.anchor: من رأى بمعنى أبصر، أو عرف، ولذلك لم يتجاوز مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāsik means their Hajj rites or slaughter places; the root means the utmost worship and became associated with Hajj for its hardship and departure from habit.
rows.anchor: متعبداتنا في الحج، أو مذابحنا. والنسك في الأصل غاية العبادة،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والسوسي عن أبي عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce arinā by analogy with fa-khid, though al-Bayḍāwī says this is strained because the kasra transferred from the dropped hamza remains as its trace.
rows.anchor: يعقوب { أرنا }.، قياسا على فخذ في فخذ، وفيه إجحاف

rows.speaker: الدوري عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Dūrī from Abū ʿAmr reads arinā with partial vowel shortening.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الدوري عن أبي عمرو بالاختلاس { وتب علينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition seeks repentance for their descendants, or for an inadvertent lapse by the two petitioners.
rows.anchor: استتابة لذريتهما، أو عما فرط منهما سهوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea may be an expression of humility and instruction for their descendants.
rows.anchor: ولعلهما قالا هضما لأنفسهما وإرشاد لذريتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one who accepts repentance from whoever repents.
rows.anchor: { إنك أنت التواب الرحيم } لمن تاب.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was the answered prayer of Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus, and his mother’s vision.
rows.anchor: " أنا دعوة إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى، ورؤيا أمي "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested messenger is from the submitted community; Muhammad was the only descendant of Abraham and Ishmael sent as such, answering their prayer.
rows.anchor: في الأمة المسلمة { رسولامنهم } ولم يبعث من ذريتهما غير محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger recites and conveys the signs God reveals, including proofs of divine unity and prophethood.
rows.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما توحي إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Book” means the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: الكتب } القرآن. { والحكمة } ما تكمل به نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom comprises the knowledge and rulings by which people’s souls are perfected.
rows.anchor: ما تكمل به نفوسهم من المعارف والأحكام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger purifies people from associating partners with God and from sins.
rows.anchor: { ويزكيهم } عن الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible in carrying out His will and perfectly orders what He wills.
rows.anchor: { إنك أنت العزيز } الذي لا يقهر ولا يغلب على ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When death comes” means when its causes have arrived and its signs have appeared.
rows.anchor: أي حضرت أسبابه وظهرت أماراته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes “good” to mean wealth generally; another takes it to mean substantial wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل مالا كثيرا، لما روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali stopped a client with 700 dirhams from making a bequest, arguing that “good” means substantial wealth.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه: أن مولى له أراد أن يوصي وله سبعمائة درهم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha told a man with 3,000 dirhams and four dependents that this was little and should be left to his family.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها: أن رجلا أراد أن يوصي فسألته كم مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waṣiyya is nominative as the subject of kutiba; the feminine verb is separated from its subject, or construed with an omitted “to bequeath” or al-īṣāʾ, matching the pronoun in “whoever changes it.”
rows.anchor: مرفوع بكتب، وتذكير فعلها للفصل، أو على تأويل أن يوصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional time expression depends on the meaning of kutiba, not on al-waṣiyya, which follows it.
rows.anchor: والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب لا الوصية لتقدمه عليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative makes al-waṣiyya a subject with “for parents” as predicate and supplies a conditional answer without fa; al-Bayḍāwī rejects it as valid only by poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وقيل مبتدأ خبره { للولدين } ، والجملة جواب الشرط بإضمار الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative syntax is illustrated by two poetic lines about God rewarding good deeds and requiting evil.
rows.anchor: من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view held that this early Islamic bequest rule was abrogated by inheritance verses and the Prophetic rule that heirs receive no bequest.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا الحكم في بدء الإسلام فنسخ بآية المواريث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said God has given each rightful person their due and that no bequest is for an heir.
rows.anchor: " إن الله أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، ألا لا وصية لوارث ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī questions abrogation: inheritance rules do not contradict the verse and can confirm priority for bequests; the solitary hadith does not become mass-transmitted merely through communal acceptance.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر: لأن آية المواريث لا تعارضه بل تؤكده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid conflict, al-waṣiyya may mean God’s command that parents and relatives inherit, or the dying person’s allocation of what God prescribed for them.
rows.anchor: من فسر الوصية بما أوصى به الله من توريث الوالدين والأقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bequests should be just: do not favor the wealthy and do not exceed one-third of the estate.
rows.anchor: بالعدل فلا يفضل الغنى، ولا يتجاوز الثلث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqqan is an emphatic verbal noun, meaning that this is truly obligatory.
rows.anchor: { حقا على المتقين } مصدر مؤكد أي حق ذلك حقا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Month of Ramadan” may be a subject followed by its predicate, the predicate of an omitted subject, or an appositive to fasting with “fast of” understood; the accusative reading supplies an imperative or object analysis, though that is weak, or apposition to the numbered days.
rows.anchor: { شهر رمضان } مبتدأ خبره ما بعده، أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Month derives from being renowned; Ramadan is a verbal noun from burning, made the month’s proper name and diptote because it is a name ending in alif and nūn.
rows.anchor: والشهر: من الشهرة، ورمضان: مصدر رمض إذا احترق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may refer to fasting in heat, burning away sins, or the hot days when month names were transferred from the old calendar.
rows.anchor: إما لارتماضهم فيه من حر الجوع والعطش، أو لارتماض الذنوب فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic phrase “fasted Ramadan” omits the word “month,” since the meaning is unambiguous.
rows.anchor: " من صام رمضان " فعلى حذف المضاف لأمن الالتباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that revelation of the Qur’an began in Ramadan on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: أي ابتدىء فيه إنزاله، وكان ذلك ليلة القدر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Qur’an descended all at once to the lowest heaven in Ramadan, then came down piecemeal to earth.
rows.anchor: أو أنزل فيه جملة إلى سماء الدنيا ثم نزل منجما إلى الأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that the Qur’an was revealed concerning Ramadan, namely the command to fast.
rows.anchor: أو أنزل في شأنه القرآن وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet dates Abraham’s scrolls to Ramadan’s first night, the Torah to its sixth, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Qur’an to its twenty-fourth.
rows.anchor: " نزلت صحف إبراهيم عليه السلام أول ليلة من رمضان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause is either the predicate or an adjective of the subject; the predicate is then “whoever witnesses,” with fa signaling its conditional sense.
rows.anchor: والموصول بصلته خبر المبتدأ أو صفته والخبر فمن شهد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That the Qur’an was revealed in Ramadan suggests revelation is why this month was singled out for obligatory fasting.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشعار بأن الإنزال فيه سبب اختصاصه بوجوب الصوم.

words: هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is guidance through its inimitability, clear proofs that guide to truth, and judgments and rulings distinguishing truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: حالان من القرآن، أن أنزل وهو هداية للناس بإعجازه وآيات واضحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever is present during the month and is not traveling must fast then; explicit mention of the month magnifies it.
rows.anchor: فمن حضر في الشهر ولم يكن مسافرا فليصم فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the main reading, “the month” is an adverb with an omitted preposition, while the second pronoun is accusative by expanded usage.
rows.anchor: لكن وضع المظهر موضع المضمر الأول للتعظيم، ونصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, witnessing means seeing the crescent, with the month as a direct object, like witnessing Friday’s prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { فمن شهد منكم } هلال الشهر فليصمه، على أنه

words: ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The make-up rule specifies the crescent interpretation, since the ill and traveler also witness the month; repetition may prevent assuming abrogation with its counterpart.
rows.anchor: مخصصا له، لأن المسافر والمريض ممن شهد الشهر ولعل تكريره لذلك،

words: يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends ease rather than hardship, so He permits breaking the fast during travel or illness.
rows.anchor: أي يريد أن ييسر عليكم ولا يعسر، فلذلك أباح الفطر في السفر والمرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clauses may explain an omitted verb for the whole ruling: completing the count concerns observing it, takbīr concerns making up missed days, and gratitude concerns the dispensation.
rows.anchor: علل لفعل محذوف دل عليه ما سبق، أي وشرع جملة ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each purpose clause may attach to its own action, to an implied rationale such as ease, or to “ease” itself.
rows.anchor: أو الأفعال كل لفعله، أو معطوفة على علة مقدرة مثل ليسهل عليكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase may coordinate with “ease,” meaning God intends ease so that you complete the count, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعطف على اليسر أي ويريد بكم لتكملوا كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination with ease is compared with the verse “They wish to extinguish God’s light,” cited as a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله [الصف: 8]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takbīr means magnifying God with praise and commendation; “upon” fits this sense.
rows.anchor: تعظيم الله بالحمد والثناء عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One alternative takes the takbīr to be the takbīr on Eid al-Fitr.
rows.anchor: وقيل تكبير يوم الفطر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another alternative takes it to be the takbīr when the new moon is sighted.
rows.anchor: وقيل التكبير عند الإهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be construed as a verbal noun, with its predicate meaning what God guided you to.
rows.anchor: وما يحتمل المصدر، والخبر أي الذي هداكم إليه

rows.speaker: عاصم برواية أبي بكر
rows.claim: In Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim, tukmilū is read with a doubled mīm.
rows.anchor: وعن عاصم برواية أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the rites and devotional acts of Hajj, worshippers are to remember God.
rows.anchor: فإذا قضيتم العبادات الحجية وفرغتم منها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should remember God abundantly, as they used to mention their fathers while boasting.
rows.anchor: فاكثروا ذكره وبالغوا فيه كما تفعلون بذكر آبائكم في المفاخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Hajj the Arabs used to stand at Minā between the mosque and mountain, recounting their ancestors’ glories and past merits.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بمنى بين المسجد والجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes “stronger remembrance” genitive coordinated with dhikr, metaphorically treating remembrance as the one who remembers.
rows.anchor: إما مجرور معطوف على الذكر يجعل الذكر ذاكرا على المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weaker alternative coordinates the phrase with its genitive complement, meaning remembrance like that of people more intense than you.
rows.anchor: أو على ما أضيف إليه على ضعف بمعنى أو كذكر قوم أشد منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing puts “stronger” in the accusative coordinated with “your fathers,” meaning more mentioned than your fathers.
rows.anchor: بالعطف على آباءكم وذكرا من فعل المذكور بمعنى أو كذكركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied command may instead mean: be more intense in remembering God than you are in remembering your fathers.
rows.anchor: أم بمضمر دل عليه المعنى تقديره: أو كونوا أشد ذكرا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshippers divide into those who seek only worldly gain through remembrance and those who seek good in both abodes; the verse urges abundant remembrance.
rows.anchor: تفصيل للذاكرين إلى مقل لا يطلب بذكر الله تعالى إلا الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly petitioner asks God to make His gift and grant theirs in this life.
rows.anchor: اجعل إيتاءنا ومنحتنا في الدنيا

words: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaq means a share or portion; such a petitioner has none in the Hereafter because his concern is confined to worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي نصيب وحظ لأن همه مقصور بالدنيا،

words: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation takes khalaq as a sought share or allotment.
rows.anchor: لأن همه مقصور بالدنيا، أو من طلب خلاق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A chronology says the earlier verse about date and grape products led Muslims to drink; Umar, Muadh, and other Companions asked about wine, and this verse followed.
rows.anchor: روي أنه نزل بمكة قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At a later banquet hosted by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, a drunken prayer prompted the prohibition on approaching prayer intoxicated.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن بن عوف ناسا منهم فشربوا وسكروا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account next describes Utban inviting Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and others; drunken boasting led Saʿd to insult the Anṣār, and an Anṣārī wounded him with a camel jaw.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا عتبان بن مالك سعد بن أبي وقاص في نفر

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After the injury and complaint, Umar prayed for a clear ruling; the final prohibition descended and he declared that they had stopped.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr comes from covering; the name applies to fermented grape or date juice because it covers the mind, as sukr names what blocks it.
rows.anchor: والخمر في الأصل مصدر خمره إذا ستره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine is categorically forbidden, as are all intoxicants according to most scholars.
rows.anchor: وهي حرام مطلقا وكذا كل ما أسكر عند أكثر العلماء.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits drinking fermented raisin or date infusion if boiled until two-thirds evaporates, provided the drinker does not become intoxicated.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى: نقيع الزبيب والتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir is a verbal noun like mawʿid; gambling is so called because it takes another’s wealth easily or strips away prosperity.
rows.anchor: سمي به القمار لأنه أخذ مال الغير بيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is about engaging in wine and gambling, as shown by the answer’s reference to what is in both.
rows.anchor: والمعنى يسألونك عن تعاطيهما لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sin consists in leading people to neglect what is commanded and commit what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: من حيث إنه يؤدي إلى الانتكاب عن المأمور، وارتكاب المحظور.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr, “much,” with thāʾ instead of kabīr, “great.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي كثير بالثاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benefits include earning money, excitement, pleasure, and companionship; wine may embolden the coward, enhance manliness, and strengthen the constitution.
rows.anchor: من كسب المال والطرب والالتذاذ ومصادقة الفتيان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harms arising from wine and gambling outweigh their expected benefits.
rows.anchor: أي المفاسد التي تنشأ منهما أعظم من المنافع المتوقعة منهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the excess of harm over benefit is what prohibits wine, since predominant harm entails prohibition; al-Bayḍāwī rejects this as reviving the Muʿtazilite doctrine previously invalidated.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قيل إنها المحرمة للخمر لأن المفسدة إذا ترجحت على المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported argument says a preponderance of harm over benefit entails that the act is prohibited.
rows.anchor: لأن المفسدة إذا ترجحت على المصلحة اقتضت تحريم الفعل،

rows.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
rows.claim: Amr ibn al-Jamuh is said to have asked first about what to spend and whom to give it to, then about how to spend.
rows.anchor: قيل سائله أيضا عمرو بن الجموح سأل أولا عن المنفق والمصرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw is the opposite of exertion: spend what is readily available without exhausting yourself.
rows.anchor: العفو نقيض الجهد ومنه يقال للأرض السهلة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses al-ʿafw in the sense of an easy or generous amount offered to preserve affection.
rows.anchor: خذي العفو مني تستديمي مودتي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet turned away from a man offering a gold egg from spoils, then tossed it and said giving all one’s wealth leaves one begging; charity is from sufficiency.
rows.anchor: إنما الصدقة عن ظهر غنى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو برفع { العفو }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” refers either to showing that surplus is better than exhausting effort or to the rulings just stated; kāf is an accusative adjective for an omitted verbal noun, and the singular is collective in sense.
rows.anchor: مثل ما بين أن العفو أصلح من الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are explained so people may reflect on the proofs and legal rulings.
rows.anchor: { لعلكم تتفكرون } في الدلائل والأحكام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputant is Nimrod; his argument and foolishness are presented as astonishing.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من محاجة نمرود وحماقته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the phrase causally: God’s granting kingship made Nimrod insolent and led him to argue.
rows.anchor: لأن آتاه أي أبطره إيتاء الملك وحمله على المحاجة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing says he argued out of gratitude for the kingship, an ironic reversal like repaying kindness with hostility.
rows.anchor: أو حاج لأجله شكرا له على طريقة العكس كقولك عاديتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes the phrase temporal: the dispute occurred when God granted Nimrod kingship.
rows.anchor: أو وقت أن آتاه الله الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal reading proves against Muʿtazilites who deny that God grants kingship to a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: وهو حجة على من منع إيتاء الله الملك الكافر من المعتزلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause may depend on ḥājja, or replace the “because He granted him kingship” phrase on the second parsing.
rows.anchor: ظرف ل { حاج } ، أو بدل من { أن آته الله الملك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives life and death by creating life and death in bodies.
rows.anchor: بخلق الحياة والموت في الأجساد.

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads rabb, omitting the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «رب» بحذف الياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod claimed to give life and death by pardoning a person sentenced to death and killing another.
rows.anchor: قال أنا أحيي وأميت } بالعفو عن القتل وبالقتل.

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads anā without the alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع «أنا» بلا ألف.

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham avoids debating Nimrod’s false equivocation and offers a clear, unanswerable example of God’s power to prevent obstruction; this changes the example, not the proof.
rows.anchor: أعرض إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام عن الاعتراض على معارضته الفاسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod may have claimed power over every kind of action God performs, which Abraham refuted with the sun’s course.
rows.anchor: ولعل نمروذ زعم أنه يقدر أن يفعل كل جنس يفعله الله فنقضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Nimrod imprisoned Abraham for days after he broke the idols, then released him to be burned and questioned him about his Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل لما كسر إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام الأصنام سجنه أياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever was left dumbfounded.
rows.anchor: فصار مبهوتا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading means that Abraham overcame the disbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { فبهت } أي فغلب إبراهيم الكافر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust are those who refuse guidance; alternatively, God does not guide them to argument, salvation, or the path to Paradise on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بالامتناع عن قبول الهداية. وقيل لا يهديهم محجة الاحتجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The teaching statement reassures Mary and removes her fear of blame for bearing a child without a husband; alternatively it coordinates with the glad tidings or describes Jesus as distinguished.
rows.anchor: كلام مبتدأ ذكر تطييبا لقلبها وإزاحة لما همها من خوف اللوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitāb may mean writing or the category of revealed books; the Torah and Gospel are singled out for their excellence.
rows.anchor: الكتبة أو جنس الكتب المنزلة. وخص الكتابان لفضلهما.

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read the verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم { ويعلمه } بالياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative “messenger” may depend on an omitted “I send him as a messenger, saying…,” or coordinate with earlier predicates while implying speech.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمضمر على إرادة القول تقديره: ويقول أرسلت رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is specified as a messenger to the Children of Israel either because his mission was limited to them or to refute claims that he was sent more broadly.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص بني إسرائيل لخصوص بعثته إليهم أو للرد على من زعم

words: أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be an appositive to “I came to you with a sign,” genitive as an appositive to “sign,” or nominative with “it is that I create.”
rows.anchor: نصب بدل من أني قد جئتكم، أو جر بدل من آية،

words: أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhluqu means to measure, form, and fashion something from clay in a shape like a bird.
rows.anchor: أقدر لكم وأصور شيئا مثل صورة الطير

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads innī with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع { إني } بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “into it” refers to the likeness, the shaped object, rather than the clay itself.
rows.anchor: الضمير للكاف أي في ذلك الشيء المماثل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shaped likeness becomes a living, flying bird by God’s command, showing that Jesus does not bring it to life independently.
rows.anchor: فيصير حيا طيارا بأمر الله، نبه به على أن إحياءه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads ṭāʾiran, with alif and hamza, here and in al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع هنا وفي المائدة «طائرا» بالألف والهمزة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akmah may mean someone born blind or someone whose eyes have been effaced.
rows.anchor: الأكمه الذي ولد أعمى أو الممسوح العين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says thousands of sick people gathered around Jesus; he went to those unable to come and treated them only by prayer.
rows.anchor: روي: أنه ربما كان يجتمع عليه ألوف من المرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “by God’s permission” blocks any inference of divinity, since reviving the dead is not a human kind of act.
rows.anchor: كرر بإذن الله دفعا لتوهم الألوهية، فإن الإحياء ليس من جنس الأفعال البشرية

words: بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus tells them unseen circumstances about themselves that they cannot doubt.
rows.anchor: بالمغيبات من أحوالكم التي لا تشكون فيها.

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign benefits those enabled to believe, or those who accept truth without obstinacy; others do not benefit from miracles.
rows.anchor: موفقين للإيمان فإن غيرهم لا ينتفع بالمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God without associating an idol or anything else with Him, whether association is overt or subtle.
rows.anchor: صنما أو غيره، أو شيئا من الإشراك جليا أو خفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to treat both parents well.
rows.anchor: وأحسنوا بهما إحسانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means people connected by kinship.
rows.anchor: } وبصاحب القرابة. { واليتمى والمسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near neighbor may be one whose dwelling is near, or one connected by kinship or religion.
rows.anchor: أي الذي قرب جواره. وقيل الذي له الجوار قرب واتصال بنسب أو دين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read in the accusative as a special construction to exalt the neighbor’s right.
rows.anchor: بالنصب على الاختصاص تعظيما لحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant neighbor is one who lives far away, or one with no kinship to the listener.
rows.anchor: البعيد، أو الذي لا قرابة له.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes three neighbors: one with rights of neighborhood, kinship, and Islam; one with neighborhood and Islam; and a non-Muslim from the People of the Book with neighborhood alone.
rows.anchor: فجار له ثلاثة حقوق: حق الجوار، وحق القرابة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion at one’s side may be a partner in learning, work, craft, or travel, or a wife.
rows.anchor: الرفيق في أمر حسن كتعلم وتصرف وصناعة وسفر، فإنه صحبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wayfarer may be a traveler or a weak person.
rows.anchor: المسافر أو الضعيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom the right hands own are enslaved men and women.
rows.anchor: العبيد والإماء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dislikes the arrogant person who turns away from relatives, neighbors, and companions, and boasts over them.
rows.anchor: متكبرا يأنف عن أقاربه وجيرانه وأصحابه ولا يلتفت إليهم.

words: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what will happen to the disbelievers among Jews, Christians, and others when God brings each nation’s witness.
rows.anchor: أي فكيف حال هؤلاء الكفرة من اليهود والنصارى وغيرهم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation’s witness is its prophet, who testifies to the corruption of their beliefs and ugliness of their deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني نبيهم يشهد على فساد عقائدهم وقبح أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad testifies to the truth of the other witnesses because he knows their communities’ beliefs and his law gathers their governing principles.
rows.anchor: تشهد على صدق هؤلاء الشهداء لعلمك بعقائدهم، واستجماع شرعك مجامع قواعدهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “These” may refer to the disbelievers whose fate is being asked about, or believers, as in the cited verse about witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقيل هؤلاء إشارة إلى الكفرة المستفهم عن حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may identify people combining disbelief and disobedience, or separately name disbelievers and disobedient people.
rows.anchor: أي يود الذين جمعوا بين الكفر وعصيان الأمر، أو الكفرة والعصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wish they could be buried with earth flat over them like the dead, or that they had never been resurrected, created, or distinguished from earth.
rows.anchor: أن يدفنوا فتسوى بهم الأرض كالموتى، أو لم يبعثوا أو لم يخلقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot conceal anything from God because their limbs testify against them.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدرون على كتمانه لأن جوارحهم تشهد عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, wāw is circumstantial: they wish the earth would cover them while unable to hide anything or deny God by claiming they were never polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل الواو للحال أي يودون أن تسوى بهم الأرض وحالهم أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after their mouths are sealed, their limbs testify, the ordeal intensifies, and they wish the earth would cover them.
rows.anchor: إذ روي: أنهم إذا قالوا ختم الله على أفواههم فتشهد عليهم جوارحهم

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read tasawwā, assimilating the first tāʾ into the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر { تسوى بهم } على أن أصله تتسوى

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read taswā by deleting the second tāʾ, from sawwaytuhu fa-tasawwā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { تسوى } على حذف التاء الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not enter prayer while intoxicated through sleep or wine until sober and understanding what you say in prayer.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقوموا إليها وأنتم سكارى من نحو نوم أو خمر

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: When wine was permitted, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf hosted Companions who drank until drunk; at Maghrib, one led prayer and recited a mistaken line, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: روي (أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله تعالى عنه صنع مأدبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “prayer” means its locations, the mosques; the point is to forbid excessive drinking and drunkenness rather than a drunk person approaching prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد بالصلاة مواضعها وهي المساجد وليس المراد منه نهي السكران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is read sukārā with fatḥa; another form may be a plural like halkā, a singular for an intoxicated people, or a collective adjective like ḥublā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { سكرى } بالفتح وسكرى على أنه جمه كهلكى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Junuban coordinates with the circumstantial clause “while you are intoxicated”; janub applies to all genders and numbers like a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله { وأنتم سكرى } إذ الجملة في موضع النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception attaches to “while junub,” exempting travel when water is unavailable and tayammum is used, as the following clause indicates.
rows.anchor: متعلق بقوله { ولا جنبا } ، استثناء من أعم الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase describes junub people, meaning “other than those passing through.”
rows.anchor: أو صفة لقوله { جنبا } أي جنبا غير عابري سبيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is evidence that tayammum does not remove the state of ritual impurity.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن التيمم لا يرفع الحدث.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If prayer means mosques, those passing through are allowed to cross while junub; al-Shāfiʿī holds this view.
rows.anchor: وجوز الجنب عبور المسجد. وبه قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa bars a junub person from passing through a mosque unless it contains water or is the route.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه: لا يجوز له المرور في المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase marks the end of the prohibition for a junub person; it also teaches worshippers to avoid distractions and purify the soul.
rows.anchor: غاية النهي عن القربان حال الجنابة، وفي الآية تنبيه على أن المصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The illness may make water use dangerous or prevent reaching it; in either case, the person is treated as lacking water.
rows.anchor: يخاف معه من استعمال الماء، فإن الواجد كالفاقد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traveler is excused when water is unavailable.
rows.anchor: على سفر } لا تجدونه فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming from the privy means becoming impure through discharge from either outlet; ghāʾiṭ originally means a low-lying place.
rows.anchor: فأحدث بخروج الخارج من أحد السبيلين، وأصل الغائط المكان المطمئن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean skin touching skin; al-Shāfiʿī uses it as evidence that touching women invalidates ablution.
rows.anchor: أو ما مسستم بشرتهن ببشرتكم، وبه استدل الشافعي على أن اللمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means sexual intercourse; lamasa is less commonly used as a euphemism for intercourse than mulāmasa.
rows.anchor: استعماله كناية عن الجماع أقل من الملامسة.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read lāmastum here and in al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي هنا وفي المائدة «لمستم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Finding no water” includes being unable to use it, since what one is barred from using counts as unavailable.
rows.anchor: فلم تتمكنوا من استعماله، إذ الممنوع عنه كالمفقود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The classification covers minor or major impurity, usually prompted by illness or travel; it names the junub case and details ordinary and incidental causes for the other.
rows.anchor: ووجه هذا التقسيم أن المترخص بالتيمم إما محدث أو جنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum means deliberately turning to clean earth; the Ḥanafīs allow hard stone, while al-Bayḍāwī’s school requires dust to adhere, reading “from it” partitively.
rows.anchor: أي فتعمدوا شيئا من وجه الأرض طاهرا. ولذلك قالت الحنفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥanafīs allow striking hard stone, while al-Bayḍāwī’s school requires dust to adhere; min in the cited verse is partitive, and treating it as a starting point is strained.
rows.anchor: فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه [المائدة 6] أي بعضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hand can mean the limb up to the shoulder, a Prophetic report of wiping to the elbows and analogy with ablution establish the limit here.
rows.anchor: وما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام تيمم ومسح يديه إلى مرفقيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness explains the eased rule and dispensation.
rows.anchor: فلذلك يسر الأمر عليكم ورخص لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means “have you not seen” with eyesight or the heart; ilā marks the endpoint because the verb includes the sense of reaching toward.
rows.anchor: من رؤية البصر أي ألم تنظر إليهم، أو القلب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients are Jewish scholars, with only a small share of Torah knowledge.
rows.anchor: حظا يسيرا من علم التوراة لأن المراد أحبار اليهود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may choose misguidance over guidance or exchange it after receiving it through knowledge of Muhammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: يختارونها على الهدى، أو يستبدلونها به بعد تمكنهم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they take bribes and distort the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يأخذون الرشى ويحرفون التوراة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They want believers to stray from the path of truth.
rows.anchor: أن تضلوا } أيها المؤمنون. { السبيل } سبيل الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who praise themselves are the People of the Book, who claimed to be God’s children and beloved.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل الكتاب قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says some Jews brought their children to the Prophet and asked if they sinned; they claimed their day and night’s sins canceled each other.
rows.anchor: ناس من اليهود جاؤوا بأطفالهم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke also applies generally to anyone who self-praises and commends themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي معناهم من زكى نفسه وأثنى عليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God’s approval counts, since He knows the good and bad concealed within people; He condemned these claimants and praised His approved believers.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على أن تزكيته تعالى هي المعتد بها دون تزكية غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of tazkiya is removing what is reprehensible in action or speech.
rows.anchor: وأصل التزكية نفي ما يستقبح فعلا أو قولا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not be wronged through blame or punishment for their unjustified self-praise.
rows.anchor: بالذم أو العقاب على تزكيتهم أنفسهم بغير حق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fatīl is a tiny thread in a date stone’s cleft, proverbial for the least and smallest injustice.
rows.anchor: أدنى ظلم وأصغره، وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains and confirms the preceding warning.
rows.anchor: كالبيان والتقرير لذلك.

words: كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same skin may be restored in a new form, like changing a ring into an earring, or its burned surface renewed so that it can again feel punishment.
rows.anchor: بأن يعاد ذلك الجلد بعينه على صورة أخرى كقولك:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed sensation lets them continue tasting the punishment.
rows.anchor: { ليذوقوا العذاب } أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه.

words: كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says a new skin is created; the actual recipient of punishment is the conscious sinful soul, not its sensory instrument, so there is no difficulty.
rows.anchor: وقيل يخلق لهم مكانه جلد آخر والعذاب في الحقيقة للنفس العاصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty: nothing can prevent what He wills.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع عليه ما يريده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise and punishes in accordance with His wisdom.
rows.anchor: { حكيما } يعاقب على وفق حكمته.
